# What a fresh install turns on

**Every pack, every preset and every rule, on or off by default**, generated from the packs and `crates/codelaw-cli/src/init.rs`, so it cannot drift: CI runs `python3 scripts/rule-docs.py --check`.

## What "on" means

- **A rule is on** when a preset that `codelaw init` writes turns it on — `<namespace>/recommended` for each pack it installs, and the few presets it adds when the repo has TypeScript, Markdown or a test framework — **and** the rule is `stable`. A project may choose other presets; a rule only they turn on is *off by default*.
- **A `preview` rule in such a preset** runs only with `preview = true` in `codelaw.toml` ([SR-RULE-PACKS](../../records/0101_rule-packs.md) decision 9). Every rule is `preview` until a corpus run promotes it, so most of what a preset names is not on yet.
- **A rule in no preset** is on only where a project names it under `[rules]`.
- **The engine's own rules** ([engine.md](engine.md)) belong to no pack and are on in every run, except the ones listed at the end.

## The engine's own rules

28 rules, 21 of them on in every run. The others:

| Rule | When it runs |
|---|---|
| `graph/untested-function` | off until `extends = ["codelaw:tests"]`, a `[coverage]` table or `[rules]` turns it on |
| `graph/function-coverage` | off until `extends = ["codelaw:tests"]`, a `[coverage]` table or `[rules]` turns it on |
| `codelaw/stale-coverage` | off until `extends = ["codelaw:tests"]`, a `[coverage]` table or `[rules]` turns it on |
| `git/commit-message` | runs only under `--changed-since`, in the `commit-msg` hook and in the agent hook |
| `git/branch-name` | runs only under `--changed-since`, in the `commit-msg` hook and in the agent hook |
| `git/pr-size` | runs only under `--changed-since`, in the `commit-msg` hook and in the agent hook |
| `git/pr-description` | runs only under `--changed-since`, in the `commit-msg` hook and in the agent hook |
